method: PARAPHRASED AND HASH-ANCHORED from ESMO and EHA Guidelines Committees (d'Amore F, Bouabdallah R, de Leval L, et al.), HemaSphere 'Peripheral T- and natural killer-cell lymphomas: ESMO-EHA Clinical Practice Guideline for diagnosis, treatment, and follow-up' (published 7 May 2025). claims.claim: **Get a surgical (excisional or incisional) biopsy where possible**; core biopsies are much less accurate for diagnosis and subtyping. (II, A)
claims.locator: ESMO and EHA Guidelines Committees (d'Amore F, Bouabdallah R, de Leval L, et al.), HemaSphere, 'Peripheral T- and natural killer-cell lymphomas: ESMO-EHA Clinical Practice Guideline for diagnosis, treatment, and follow-up', published 7 May 2025, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC12059256/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **PTCL is rare and hard to diagnose**, so an expert haematopathologist with all slides and at least 1 tissue block should make or confirm the diagnosis. Treatment differs by entity.
claims.locator: ESMO and EHA Guidelines Committees (d'Amore F, Bouabdallah R, de Leval L, et al.), HemaSphere, 'Peripheral T- and natural killer-cell lymphomas: ESMO-EHA Clinical Practice Guideline for diagnosis, treatment, and follow-up', published 7 May 2025, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC12059256/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Discuss every patient in a PTCL-experienced multidisciplinary team.** (I, A)
claims.locator: ESMO and EHA Guidelines Committees (d'Amore F, Bouabdallah R, de Leval L, et al.), HemaSphere, 'Peripheral T- and natural killer-cell lymphomas: ESMO-EHA Clinical Practice Guideline for diagnosis, treatment, and follow-up', published 7 May 2025, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC12059256/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Baseline tests:** full blood count, LDH, uric acid, renal and liver function, immunoglobulins, and HIV, hepatitis B and C and EBV serology (HTLV-1 in ATLL).
claims.locator: ESMO and EHA Guidelines Committees (d'Amore F, Bouabdallah R, de Leval L, et al.), HemaSphere, 'Peripheral T- and natural killer-cell lymphomas: ESMO-EHA Clinical Practice Guideline for diagnosis, treatment, and follow-up', published 7 May 2025, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC12059256/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **PET-CT is the preferred imaging** at diagnosis and end of treatment (I, B), with CT if PET is unavailable. A bone marrow biopsy is recommended in every case (I, A), and re-biopsy at relapse (I, A).
claims.locator: ESMO and EHA Guidelines Committees (d'Amore F, Bouabdallah R, de Leval L, et al.), HemaSphere, 'Peripheral T- and natural killer-cell lymphomas: ESMO-EHA Clinical Practice Guideline for diagnosis, treatment, and follow-up', published 7 May 2025, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC12059256/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Offer a clinical trial whenever possible.** (II, A)
claims.locator: ESMO and EHA Guidelines Committees (d'Amore F, Bouabdallah R, de Leval L, et al.), HemaSphere, 'Peripheral T- and natural killer-cell lymphomas: ESMO-EHA Clinical Practice Guideline for diagnosis, treatment, and follow-up', published 7 May 2025, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC12059256/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **CHOP (or CHOP-like, such as CHOEP) is standard** for non-ALCL nodal types despite poor outcomes; nothing has beaten it. (II, B)
claims.locator: ESMO and EHA Guidelines Committees (d'Amore F, Bouabdallah R, de Leval L, et al.), HemaSphere, 'Peripheral T- and natural killer-cell lymphomas: ESMO-EHA Clinical Practice Guideline for diagnosis, treatment, and follow-up', published 7 May 2025, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC12059256/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Brentuximab-CHP did not improve outcomes in PTCL-NOS or TFHL** in the randomised trial (few such patients were enrolled), and is not EU-approved for them.
claims.locator: ESMO and EHA Guidelines Committees (d'Amore F, Bouabdallah R, de Leval L, et al.), HemaSphere, 'Peripheral T- and natural killer-cell lymphomas: ESMO-EHA Clinical Practice Guideline for diagnosis, treatment, and follow-up', published 7 May 2025, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC12059256/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Limited-stage, non-bulky, favourable-risk disease:** a shortened course of three or four cycles (CHOP or CHOEP) can suffice (IV, B), optionally followed by involved-site radiotherapy of 30-40 Gy in 15-20 fractions (IV, B).
claims.locator: ESMO and EHA Guidelines Committees (d'Amore F, Bouabdallah R, de Leval L, et al.), HemaSphere, 'Peripheral T- and natural killer-cell lymphomas: ESMO-EHA Clinical Practice Guideline for diagnosis, treatment, and follow-up', published 7 May 2025, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC12059256/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Autologous transplant consolidation can be considered** for responders whose disease is advanced, or limited but high-risk (III, B); it is acceptable in chemosensitive disease.
claims.locator: ESMO and EHA Guidelines Committees (d'Amore F, Bouabdallah R, de Leval L, et al.), HemaSphere, 'Peripheral T- and natural killer-cell lymphomas: ESMO-EHA Clinical Practice Guideline for diagnosis, treatment, and follow-up', published 7 May 2025, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC12059256/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Six cycles of brentuximab vedotin with CHP are recommended for chemotherapy-eligible ALCL, ALK-positive or ALK-negative** (I, A); CHO(E)P for six cycles is an alternative (III, B).
claims.locator: ESMO and EHA Guidelines Committees (d'Amore F, Bouabdallah R, de Leval L, et al.), HemaSphere, 'Peripheral T- and natural killer-cell lymphomas: ESMO-EHA Clinical Practice Guideline for diagnosis, treatment, and follow-up', published 7 May 2025, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC12059256/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **In the randomised trial, BV-CHP beat CHOP in ALCL:** 5-year PFS 51.4% versus 43.0%, and 5-year OS 70.1% versus 61.0%.
claims.locator: ESMO and EHA Guidelines Committees (d'Amore F, Bouabdallah R, de Leval L, et al.), HemaSphere, 'Peripheral T- and natural killer-cell lymphomas: ESMO-EHA Clinical Practice Guideline for diagnosis, treatment, and follow-up', published 7 May 2025, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC12059256/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Limited-stage, non-bulky ALCL with IPI 0-1:** a shortened course of three or four cycles (BV-CHP or CHOEP) is an option. (III, B)
claims.locator: ESMO and EHA Guidelines Committees (d'Amore F, Bouabdallah R, de Leval L, et al.), HemaSphere, 'Peripheral T- and natural killer-cell lymphomas: ESMO-EHA Clinical Practice Guideline for diagnosis, treatment, and follow-up', published 7 May 2025, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC12059256/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Transplant in first CR:** consider autologous transplant for eligible, chemosensitive ALK-negative ALCL (II, B). Generally not for ALK-positive ALCL (III, D), unless high-risk (IPI 2 or more, bulky) without CR after three cycles (III, B).
claims.locator: ESMO and EHA Guidelines Committees (d'Amore F, Bouabdallah R, de Leval L, et al.), HemaSphere, 'Peripheral T- and natural killer-cell lymphomas: ESMO-EHA Clinical Practice Guideline for diagnosis, treatment, and follow-up', published 7 May 2025, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC12059256/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Prognosis is poor** (median PFS 3.1 months and OS 5.5 months in one study), so enter a clinical trial whenever possible. (II, A)
claims.locator: ESMO and EHA Guidelines Committees (d'Amore F, Bouabdallah R, de Leval L, et al.), HemaSphere, 'Peripheral T- and natural killer-cell lymphomas: ESMO-EHA Clinical Practice Guideline for diagnosis, treatment, and follow-up', published 7 May 2025, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC12059256/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Outside a trial, use a platinum-based regimen not cross-resistant with first-line anthracycline chemotherapy** (for example ICE, DHAP, GDP). Frailer patients can have lenalidomide, bendamustine or ciclosporin. (III, B)
claims.locator: ESMO and EHA Guidelines Committees (d'Amore F, Bouabdallah R, de Leval L, et al.), HemaSphere, 'Peripheral T- and natural killer-cell lymphomas: ESMO-EHA Clinical Practice Guideline for diagnosis, treatment, and follow-up', published 7 May 2025, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC12059256/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Transplant responders:** for eligible patients who respond to salvage, allogeneic transplant is preferred if not used first line; it is the best curative option, with about 50% 5-year survival in retrospective series. (II, B)
claims.locator: ESMO and EHA Guidelines Committees (d'Amore F, Bouabdallah R, de Leval L, et al.), HemaSphere, 'Peripheral T- and natural killer-cell lymphomas: ESMO-EHA Clinical Practice Guideline for diagnosis, treatment, and follow-up', published 7 May 2025, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC12059256/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Romidepsin and pralatrexate as single agents** have conditional FDA approval only (not EMA), and romidepsin, like several other single agents, gives response rates under 40% with few lasting responses.
claims.locator: ESMO and EHA Guidelines Committees (d'Amore F, Bouabdallah R, de Leval L, et al.), HemaSphere, 'Peripheral T- and natural killer-cell lymphomas: ESMO-EHA Clinical Practice Guideline for diagnosis, treatment, and follow-up', published 7 May 2025, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC12059256/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Relapsed ALK-negative ALCL:** salvage chemotherapy (ICE, DHAP, GDP, IVAC-MTX) or brentuximab monotherapy (III, B).
claims.locator: ESMO and EHA Guidelines Committees (d'Amore F, Bouabdallah R, de Leval L, et al.), HemaSphere, 'Peripheral T- and natural killer-cell lymphomas: ESMO-EHA Clinical Practice Guideline for diagnosis, treatment, and follow-up', published 7 May 2025, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC12059256/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Relapsed ALK-positive ALCL:** brentuximab if not used first line or after a late relapse (III, A); if refractory to it, an ALK inhibitor such as crizotinib (III, A). Consolidate responders with allogeneic transplant (III, A).
claims.locator: ESMO and EHA Guidelines Committees (d'Amore F, Bouabdallah R, de Leval L, et al.), HemaSphere, 'Peripheral T- and natural killer-cell lymphomas: ESMO-EHA Clinical Practice Guideline for diagnosis, treatment, and follow-up', published 7 May 2025, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC12059256/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Review with history and examination every 3 months for 1 year, then every 6 months for 2 more years** (4 more after autologous transplant) (IV, C). Routine surveillance scans in CR are not recommended (III, D).
claims.locator: ESMO and EHA Guidelines Committees (d'Amore F, Bouabdallah R, de Leval L, et al.), HemaSphere, 'Peripheral T- and natural killer-cell lymphomas: ESMO-EHA Clinical Practice Guideline for diagnosis, treatment, and follow-up', published 7 May 2025, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC12059256/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Follow-up can stop** after 3 years if not transplanted and asymptomatic, or after 5 years after autologous transplant, if still in CR. (III, B)
claims.locator: ESMO and EHA Guidelines Committees (d'Amore F, Bouabdallah R, de Leval L, et al.), HemaSphere, 'Peripheral T- and natural killer-cell lymphomas: ESMO-EHA Clinical Practice Guideline for diagnosis, treatment, and follow-up', published 7 May 2025, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC12059256/, retrieved 2026-09-23
